title: A LAND NOT TO BE DEFILED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not accept a ransom for anyone who has fled to a city of refuge and so allow them to go back and live on their own land before the death of the high priest. Do not pollute the land where you are. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and atonement cannot be made for the land on which blood has been shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it. Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell, for I, the Lord, dwell among the Israelites.'" - Num 35:32-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God concludes with a weighty statement about the land itself. Bloodshed, He says, pollutes the land, and unjust bloodshed left unaddressed defiles the very place where His people live. And here is the heart of it: "I, the Lord, dwell among the Israelites." God dwelt among His people, and because His presence was there, the land had to be kept from defilement. Sin was not merely a private matter; it affected the place where the holy God had chosen to dwell.

This tells us how seriously God takes holiness where He is present. He is a holy God, and He dwells among a people who must therefore take sin seriously. Unaddressed evil corrupts the community and grieves the God who dwells there. His presence is a gift, but it also calls His people to holiness.

Under the new covenant, something astonishing has happened: God now dwells not in a land or a temple of stone, but in His people by His Spirit. Paul says our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19), and that we together are being built into a dwelling in which God lives (Eph 2:22). The God who once dwelt among Israel now dwells within believers through Christ.

This makes holiness a matter of the heart, close and personal. Because God's Spirit dwells in us, we are called to keep our lives from defilement, not to earn His presence but because He is already present. And the only atonement that can truly cleanse is the blood of Christ, which purifies us completely (1 John 1:7). We keep ourselves pure out of reverence and gratitude, mindful that the holy God has made His home in us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does it change how you live to know God's Spirit dwells within you?
2. Are there areas of "defilement" you need to bring to Christ for cleansing?
3. How does reverence for God's presence shape your pursuit of holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Lord, thank You that by Your Spirit You dwell within me through Christ. Help me to keep my life pure out of reverence and gratitude, and cleanse me thoroughly by the blood of Jesus. Amen.
